expected_reuse: The revised program applies across taxpayers, years, positive or negated claims, and incomplete records. It can prove §63(c)(3) amounts either by summing expressly given §63(f) component entitlements—covering the supervised $600-plus-$600 case without demanding unstated prerequisites—or by deriving all possible totals from primitive age, blindness, marital, survivor, and spouse-exemption facts.
learning_object: Revised executable tri-valued policy for §63(c)(6)(A) applicability and §63(c)(3) additional-standard-deduction amount claims. It now treats expressly stated §63(f) entitlements or amounts as case premises and sums those components directly, while retaining source-based derivation from age, blindness, marital status, and spouse-exemption facts when no entitlement is given.
remaining_unknown: Claims concerning taxable income, the basic standard deduction, dependent caps, §63(c)(6)(B) or (D), and other portions of §63 remain unsupported.
The supplied law does not contain the complete §152 dependent definition; expressly stated dependency is therefore treated as a case fact.
When neither component entitlements nor their underlying facts are stated, the amount remains unknown rather than treating missing events as false.
The prototype does not reconstruct every marital-status exception under §7703, including the full married-living-apart test.

source_rules.quote: a married individual filing a separate return where either spouse itemizes deductions
For purposes of paragraph (1), the additional standard deduction is the sum of each additional amount to which the taxpayer is entitled under subsection (f).

The taxpayer shall be entitled to an additional amount of $600-

        (A) for himself if he has attained age 65 before the close of his taxable year, and

        (B) for the spouse of the taxpayer if the spouse has attained age 65 before the close of the taxable year and an additional exemption is allowable to the taxpayer for such spouse under section 151(b).

The taxpayer shall be entitled to an additional amount of $600-

        (A) for himself if he is blind at the close of the taxable year, and

        (B) for the spouse of the taxpayer if the spouse is blind as of the close of the taxable year and an additional exemption is allowable to the taxpayer for such spouse under section 151(b).
In the case of an individual who is not married and is not a surviving spouse, paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be applied by substituting "$750" for "$600".

an additional exemption of the exemption amount for the spouse of the taxpayer if a joint return is not made by the taxpayer and his spouse, and if the spouse, for the calendar year in which the taxable year of the taxpayer begins, has no gross income and is not the dependent of another taxpayer.
whose spouse died during either of the two years immediately preceding the taxable year
